Paragraph: Summary of Passage: A person whose endeavors are free from selfish desire and whose reactions are burnt by the fire of knowledge is recognized by sages as truly wise.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Self-serving cravings corrupting motivation and burdening the mind with continuous anxiety over rewards.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna declares: 'yasya sarve samarambhah kama-sankalpa-varjitah, jnanagni-dagdha-karmanam tam ahuh panditam budhah' (One whose undertakings are free from desire for gratification, and whose work is burned by the fire of knowledge, is called a wise sage).
Outcome/Resolution: Purifies human motivation, establishing that selflessness burns away psychological burden and karmic baggage.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Purity of Motivation: Acting out of duty and service rather than egoic cravings
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Burnout Prevention: Eliminating emotional fatigue by dissolving selfish expectations
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Cognitive Mastery: Using wisdom to dissolve residual mental stress and past regrets

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Kama-sankalpa-varjitah (Free from selfish desire and self-centered intent)
Jnanagni-dagdha-karmanam (Actions burned up by the fire of wisdom)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: When work is performed without personal longing, spiritual knowledge burns away all karmic consequences, elevating the practitioner to steady wisdom.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Removing selfish agendas from your work prevents anxiety, allowing clear knowledge to burn away mental stress and baggage.
